test_title: SSC MTS 2024 Official Paper (Held On: 11 Nov, 2024 Shift 3)
subject: general
question:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.

If I wrote an email / to my boss now, / he will react / by yelling at me tomorrow in the morning.

options.text: by yelling at me tomorrow in the morning.

solution:
The correct answer is **Option 4: If I wrote an email**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The error lies in the phrase "**If I wrote an email**." The conditional sentence is in the past tense ("wrote"), but the result clause is in the future tense ("will react"), which creates a mismatch in verb tenses.

 
 
• **Correct form:** "If I **were** to write an email" (using the past subjunctive form "were" to indicate a hypothetical situation).
 
 
 
• **"If I were to write an email"** correctly uses the past subjunctive ("were") in a hypothetical situation, as we are discussing a potential event in the future, not something that already happened.

Therefore, the correct answer is: **Option 4: If I wrote an email**.

 

**Complete Sentence:** *If I were__ to write an email to my boss now, he will react by yelling at me tomorrow in the morning.*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1: "to my boss now,"** (no error): This segment is correct as it clearly indicates the intended recipient of the email.
 
• **Option 2: "he will react"** (no error): This segment correctly uses the future tense, which is appropriate for the reaction to the hypothetical email.
 
• **Option 3: "by yelling at me tomorrow in the morning."** (no error): This segment is grammatically correct and properly indicates the manner of reaction (yelling) along with the time frame ("tomorrow in the morning").
